A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shampoo study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Imagewoof experiments, AlgoPerf workload results, and eigenvalue/eigenbasis ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds architecture controls and eigenbasis-update analyses for a Llama 3 model trained on C4.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds an untested adaptation for Shampoo without full eigenvalue correction: reuse the eigenbasis while refreshing factor eigenvalues from projected current factors. The central EShampoo procedure and adaptive criterion remain unchanged; new Algorithm 2 primarily documents the practical implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds language-model training on C4 for the eigenbasis analysis in Appendix E.2 and Figure 8, substantially extending coverage beyond the existing Imagewoof and AlgoPerf workloads. All previously evaluated datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets, including AdamW, Shampoo variants, the SOAP-style QR configuration, and NAdamW in the ImageNet curves. Newly discussed Muon and KL-Shampoo are not added as evaluated baselines. New Figures 7–8 compare parameter groups and architectures.

E3.justification: New diagnostics remove learnable ViT layer-normalization parameters and train a 324M-parameter Llama 3 on 3.2B tokens with F = 1 and tau = 0.01. Appendix E.1 adds 6e-4 to the stated ViT trace-scaled Shampoo2 learning-rate grid. Section 4.3 changes tau from 0.01 to 0.1, conflicting with the retained Figure 4 caption; an actual rerun is not established. AlgoPerf protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 substantially extends the investigation of adaptive-update patterns: a layer-normalization parameter ablation, a ConvNeXt V2 analysis, and C4 analyses separating normalization, attention, MLP, embedding, and output parameters. These test the generality and possible compensation mechanisms behind v1's Imagewoof ViT observations.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain the same run counts and mean/standard-error reporting. The new diagnostic plots continue Figure 4's practice of summarizing variation across preconditioners or parameter groups. No new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing protocol is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 7–8 add substantive architecture- and modality-dependent findings. Removing learnable layer-normalization parameters leaves L_t/R_t update counts approximately unchanged; on C4, L_t updates more frequently than normalization-factor A_t, unlike Imagewoof. Embedding L_t/R_t frequencies are nearly equal, and attention/MLP patterns are similar. Existing benchmark values, loss curves, and Figure 6's heatmap remain unchanged; these are added diagnostic results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly states p > 0 in the main-text lemma and corrects the scaling-matrix dimensions and exponent assignments when identifying Shampoo instances. Appendix A changes the stated regime of the original regret analysis from nonconvex to convex. The principal bounds, proofs, and basis-aware correction derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: explaining grafting through eigenvalue scaling/staleness, removing its necessity through eigenvalue correction, and adaptively controlling eigenbasis approximation error. The added evidence and wording changes do not materially redefine those claims.

C2.justification: Figure 7 adds the interpretation that removing learnable layer-normalization parameters produces no compensatory L_t/R_t updating. Section 3 expands discussion of memory-saving alternatives through RMS rescaling and per-factor eigenvalue correction. Existing limitations concerning larger-model scaling, approximation quality, and regret guarantees remain.

D1.justification: New practical Algorithm 2 specifies momentum, bias correction, weight decay, basis initialization, update timing, and AdamW behavior before the first basis update. Appendix B distinguishes EShampoo from SOAP's implementation. Appendix E adds an implementation-access link and details the new language-model configuration, including gradient blocking at dimension 8192. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion and citations for KL-Shampoo, Muon scaling, earlier observations about frequent early eigenbasis updates, alternative interpretations of optimization, and the C4/Llama resources. It also sharpens the relationship between practical EShampoo and SOAP. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, and Sections 3–5 undergo extensive sentence and paragraph rewriting, condensation, and explanatory reorganization. Terminology now separates generic eigenvalue-corrected Shampoo from practical EShampoo. Appendix B is expanded around idealized versus practical algorithms, and a new experimental subsection is inserted.

P2.justification: v2 adds two multipanel diagnostic figures and a practical pseudocode block, clarifies several captions, and compacts the author block. The original benchmark Figures 7–9 are retained as Figures 9–11 with unchanged graphics. Existing tables and other plots are largely preserved, with local layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through practical pseudocode and implementation-access information, while new controls and C4 diagnostics strengthen the assessment of where update-pattern findings generalize. These are useful incremental gains; central claims and benchmark performance evidence remain unchanged. The newly introduced tau inconsistency between Section 4.3 and Figure 4 slightly offsets the improved clarity.
